name: Machine preacher curl
cue: Keep your upper arms on the pad and lower all the way.
research: research.json biomech.preacher_curl: seated, trunk 10 deg forward, hips ~100, knees 90, feet flat. Backs of the upper arms on a pad sloping 45 deg from vertical (shoulder flexion 55 relative to the trunk, abduction ~9), elbows at the pad's lower end, elbow 10 -> 120 with the upper arm still. Supinated grip. Each handle rides on a lever whose hinge IS that elbow's hinge axis (elbow joint centre, axis 5 deg off X because of the abduction; tools/design/preacher_curl.mjs), so the handle path is exactly the forearm arc. The levers run on the inner side of each forearm from hubs between the elbows, so from the side camera they hide behind the forearms and never cross the biceps. The pad runs from the armpit to just above the elbow (0.153 H) and is placed 3 mm into the back of the arm, so its carve seats the triceps on it. Hubs, bearing, hanger and lever arms use the matte plate finish so no machine highlight sits against the biceps. The ends that face the sky at the peak are closed with matte parts: a rounded knuckle on each lever-arm end, a thin cap on each outer handle end and a cap where the beam meets the column (they read as pale discs above the fists; machine luminance P99.9 at the peak 0.34 -> 0.15, pixels above the glow P90 146 -> 20). Load: a cam on the lever axle between the elbows winds a cable that runs inside the beam and the column to a guided weight stack in front of the column (it rises with the curl, 0.032 H of cable per radian), so the machine reads as loaded from the side.

camera.note: Research view az 90 / el 10; turned 10 deg toward the front and raised 6 deg (az 80 / el 16) so the near biceps reads as the dominant oval in the V between upper arm and forearm at the peak, with the far biceps smaller above it. From the true profile the two biceps sat side by side on the front of the chest and read like a chest glow. Fill 0.62: the seated figure is short, and a larger arm reads better on a phone. The machine stands on a floor rail from the seat post, the column foot and a foot plate under the feet (a plate under everything ran under the exercise name on the phone).
